rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance (San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 11)
rules.requirement: Bans selling, licensing or providing algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy levels to landlords, and bans landlords from using them to set rents or occupancy for residential rental property. Tenants may sue for injunctive relief, damages or civil penalties.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation
rules.penalty: Tenant civil action: injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.status_basis: Document is a proposed ordinance with final passage date blank; takes effect on the thirtieth day after final passage.

requires.name: residential_rental_property
requires.text: residential rental property in the City of San Diego

exempt_if.name: aggregated_reports
exempt_if.text: A software or product used by a person to publish reports regarding rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data that is more than 90 days old, or from information available to the general public, and does not recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for future residential rental property leases or renewals.

exempt_if.name: affordable_housing_program_software
exempt_if.text: A software or product used by a person to establish rental rates or income limits in accordance with local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.

coverage.summary: Applies to sellers of algorithmic devices and landlords using them for residential rental property in San Diego.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Excludes aggregated reports from public or 90-day-old historical data and software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.

rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord. (b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
